keyVerseText: And will be a Father unto you, and ye shall be my sons and daughters, saith the Lord Almighty.
rootMeaning: The word παντοκράτωρ (pantokrátōr) is formed from the Greek roots πᾶς (pâs), meaning 'all' or 'every,' and κράτος (krátos), meaning 'power' or 'strength.' Thus, its literal meaning is 'the one who has all power' or 'all-ruler.' This root sense emphasizes not just power, but comprehensive, universal authority over all things, which enriches the common English glosses of 'Almighty' or 'Omnipotent' by highlighting the totality and sovereignty inherent in the term.
usageInScripture: The term παντοκράτωρ appears ten times in Scripture, predominantly translated as 'Almighty' seven times, with a few instances as 'the Almighty,' 'omnipotent,' or 'of Almighty.' This consistent translation underscores the concept of God as the absolute and universal sovereign, a ruler whose authority is unmatched and all-encompassing. The usage in both the Old Testament (LXX) and New Testament contexts reflects a continuity in portraying God as the all-powerful ruler, affirming His supreme dominion.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding παντοκράτωρ as the 'all-ruler' deepens our appreciation of God's sovereign power and authority over creation. This word reveals that God's might is not partial or limited but absolute and universal, affirming His ability to govern all things according to His will. For the Christian faith, this assures believers of God's ultimate control and providential care, encouraging trust and reverence. It also highlights the uniqueness of God as the only true sovereign, distinguishing Him from any earthly power or authority. Recognizing God as παντοκράτωρ invites believers into a relationship of submission and confidence in His almighty power.
keyVerseReflection: In 2 Corinthians 6:18, God declares, 'And will be a Father unto you, and ye shall be my sons and daughters, saith the Lord Almighty.' The use of παντοκράτωρ here enriches the promise by affirming that the Father who adopts believers is the all-powerful sovereign God. This assures believers that their adoption is under the authority and protection of the One who rules over all, providing both intimacy and security in their relationship with Him.
